search_space: Exhaustively swept all 36 ordered pairs (A,B) of 2-element subsets of the fixed labeled universe {x_1,x_2,x_3,x_4}, with n=4 and S_1=S_k equal to that universe, in itertools.combinations lexicographic order.
witness_description: Let n=4 and S_1=S_k={x_1,x_2,x_3,x_4}. Choose A={x_1,x_2} from S_1 and B={x_3,x_4} from S_k. Each choice has exactly n/2=2 elements, but A and B are disjoint.
refutation_explanation: The stated premise is satisfied, yet no x_i is chosen from both sets. Choosing n elements in total from a universe of n possible elements does not by itself force a repeated element; the pigeonhole principle would require more than n selections.
